analysis:
All changes are CI workflow and composite-action files. None touch the provider runtime, the coordinator WebSocket contract, keys, attestation, App Attest or the prefix-cache code that the canonical threat model covers (T-041 and others), so I found no regression against those threat IDs.

Examined:
- provider-ci-build/action.yml: the SwiftPM repository cache and the Metal cache move to fixed /private/tmp/dinf-ci paths, and a symlink is created from the home-directory cache into that path. Saves still happen only when save-caches=='true' (trusted pushes). Cache keys are unchanged. Residual CI-hygiene question: /private/tmp/dinf-ci is a fixed shared path. If self-hosted macOS hosts are persistent and shared between jobs, one job could influence another's cache contents. I have no evidence of that deployment; the Darkbloom and Blacksmith runners appear to be per-job VMs. This is not a threat-model asset.
- provider-ci-products/action.yml (new): build-to-test artifact handoff. Actions are pinned by SHA, artifacts are scoped to the current run (download-artifact with no run-id), and retention is 1 day. Lane and direction inputs are validated against an allowlist and passed through env rather than interpolated into shell. The security of the handoff depends on scripts/ci-test-products.py (pack, unpack, toolchain check), which was not supplied. Archive extraction safety (path traversal, symlinks) and artifact integrity between jobs are therefore unverified.
- darkbloom-route.yml: the new optional size and required fields are strictly regex-validated (<vCPUs>x<GiB>, macOS only). Runner labels are accepted only when the plane's runs_on exactly equals the profile array with the size suffix on the last label, so untrusted plane text cannot select arbitrary labels. The output still uses $decision.runs_on only after that equality check. A size is sent only if DARKBLOOM_JOB_SHAPES is 'on', and required lanes fall back when sizes are off. The new request echo contains only the repository, run id, attempt and lanes, with no secrets. Fork-PR and routing-off fallbacks are preserved.
- provider-plan.yml: only the lane table changes, adding sizes and required flags and reordering.

Remaining question for integration: confirm that scripts/ci-test-products.py unpack validates archive members and the toolchain before executing the products.
